title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol: first inconvenience fails — electing Peter/Paul to infallible share of Christ before foreseeing free will inclined is supreme love of justice, not loving them more than justice
pass_a_gloss: This being premised, our sentence is by no means implicated in the aforesaid two inconveniences. Not in the former; Because God is not argued to have loved Peter or Paul more than his own justice, if from eternity he elected and designated them unto the infallible participation of Christ, of faith, and of salvation, before he foresaw their free choice efficaciously and perseveringly inclined through the offer of sufficient grace unto embracing Christ, conceiving faith, and taking the way of salvation. Nay, this argues the supreme love of justice in God, that Peter and Paul, whom of mere mercy he exceedingly loved unto salvation, he yet would not lead unto this salvation destined for them unless such means were applied by which his justice would first be satisfied.
pass_b_english: That premised, our view is not caught in those two inconveniences. Not the first: God is not charged with loving Peter or Paul more than his own justice if from eternity he elected and designated them to infallible share in Christ, faith, and salvation before he foresaw their free choice efficaciously and perseveringly inclined — through the offer of sufficient grace — to embrace Christ, conceive faith, and take the way of salvation. Nay, this argues supreme love of justice in God: that Peter and Paul, whom of mere mercy he loved exceedingly unto salvation, he yet would not lead to that destined salvation unless such means were used by which his justice would first be satisfied.
source_text: Hoc praemisso, sententia nostra praedictis duobus incommodis haud implicatur. Non priore; Quia Deus non arguitur magis amasse Petrum aut Paulum quam suam justitiam, si illos ab aeterno elegit et designavit ad infallibilem participationem Christi, fidei, et salutis, antequam praevidit liberum illorum arbitrium per oblationem gratiae sufficientis ad Christum amplexandum, fidem concipiendam, salutisque viam capiessendam, efficaciter et perseveranter inclinatum. Imo hoc arguit summum amorem justitiae in Deo, quod Petrum et Paulum, quos ad salutem ex mera misericordia eximie dilexit, noluerit tamen ad hanc salutem illis destinatam perducere nisi talibus mediis adhibitis quibus justitiae suae prius satisfaceret.
